newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-PIOLINE, RIOS OUT OF SWISS OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIOLINE, RIOS OUT OF SWISS OPEN.

text.p: Wimbledon finalist Cedric Pioline and fourth seed Marcelo Rios were second round casualties at the Swiss Open on Thursday.
Pioline, the first Frenchman since 1946 to reach the Wimbledon final, was trailing second seeded Alex Corretja of Spain 2-6 2-3 when he was forced to abandon the match because of a sore right arm.

"My arm just doesn't feel like holding a racket right now," said Pioline, who twice received treatment during changeovers before retiring. "It's just tired from too many serves, too much this and too much that.
"I don't think it will take long to get better. It's not that type of injury."
Pioline said he would return to action at the Canadian Open on July 28.
Any discomfort Rios felt on court was provided by little known Spaniard Juan Albert Viloca, who swept aside the world number nine 6-3 7-6 (7-3).
While it was Viloca's first ever win over a top 10 player, it was the second time in three meetings that he had beaten the moody Chilean.
"That guy, sometimes he plays unbelievable and if he's playing well he's difficult to beat," said Viloca. "I beat him before but then he was number 11, so this is a good win for me."
Typically, Rios had no explanation for his erratic performance against a player ranked 58 places below him, saying only, "sometimes you don't feel like playing and today was one of those days."
Viloca will now meet wildcard Nicolas Kiefer, the rising star of German tennis, in the quarterfinals.
Kiefer, ranked 68 in the world, one spot below Viloca, advanced with a 7-5 6-3 win over American Richey Reneberg, who had upset defending champion Albert Costa in the first round.

Seventh seed Alberto Berasategui set up an all-Spanish quarter-final clash with Corettja by prevailing 7-6 (7-2) 1-6 7-5 over Italy's Renzo Furlan in a seesaw battle that was twice interrupted by rain.
